Title: Guan Eng questions Penang PH silence over Reezal's remarks
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today questioned Penang PH leaders' silence over Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican's remarks on Umno-DAP ties.
Lim said Penang PH's unconditional endorsement of Umno's role in the state government, without responding to Reezal's remarks, was "incomprehensible".
"Penang PH top leaders' unconditional endorsement of Umno's role in the Penang government without any response to the unfriendly attacks by the Umno Bertam assemblyman on DAP and PKR is incomprehensible," he said today.
Reezal had denied that BN exploited identity politics during the Negri Sembilan election.
Instead, Lim said, Reezal had made baseless allegations that DAP and PKR had focused only on a single race.
Lim questioned why Penang PH leaders had failed to rebut what he described as unprovoked and unjustified allegations while approving Umno's continued role in the Penang government.
"Penang PH top leaders' failure to rebut these unprovoked and unjustified allegations while approving Umno's continued role in the Penang government would raise the following query.
"How does this approach by the political leadership in Penang PH send a message to our voters of decisively defending our honour and dignity as the Penang government and as elected leaders?" he asked.
Penang PH has reaffirmed its electoral cooperation with BN, saying the partnership remains important ahead of the next general election.
Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said the state
coalition
had agreed to retain the BN executive councillor in the Penang government, in line with the understanding reached during the 2023 election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four laws to reshape Malaysia's housing sector under new policy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is set to overhaul Malaysia's housing landscape with four new and amended laws under the newly launched National Housing Policy 2026-2035.
Its minister Nga Kor Ming said the legislative reforms were aimed at modernising oversight of property development, strata living and the rental market to ensure long-term stability.
The four legislative measures are an expanded Property Development Act, a new Building Managers Act, a new Residential Tenancy Act and amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013.
Speaking at a press conference after the launch of the National Housing Policy today, Nga said the existing Housing Development (Control and Licensing) Act 1966 (Act 118) was no longer sufficient as its scope was limited to residential properties.
"The current act does not extend to commercial properties, shop lots, or commercial projects. This new act (Property Development Act) will provide a comprehensive legal framework to move the country forward," he said.
Nga also highlighted the need for more robust management of high-rise developments.
With Malaysia's urbanisation rate projected to reach 85 per cent by 2040, he said a "progressive legal framework" was needed to manage the complexities of high-density living.
To address this, the ministry will introduce the Building Managers Act and amend the Strata Management Act 2013.
Nga said Malaysia currently had nearly three million strata units across more than 27,000 schemes, including condominiums and SoHos
"It is vital that the maintenance and safety of these buildings are kept at a high standard," Nga said.
On the Residential Tenancy Act, Nga said the proposed law aimed to create a more equitable environment by balancing the interests of landlords and tenants.
"Tenants have rights, and owners have rights. This Act will protect everyone's interests," he said, adding that it was expected to include safeguards against arbitrary rent increases and ensure due legal process was followed during unit repossessions.
Nga had said in February
that the reforms were anchored on five core principles under the 13th Malaysia Plan, aimed at ensuring affordability, sustainability and market stability.
Also present at the launch were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Attorney-General Tan Sri Muhammad Dusuki Mokhtar and National Housing Department director-general Dr Tan Awang Besar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: German shippers warn Rhine could be 'split in two' by low water
Article:
BERLIN: Low water levels risk halting cargo traffic on a key stretch of the Rhine this week, effectively splitting the critical waterway into two separate zones, the federal association of German inland shipping (BDB) said on Monday.
BDB managing director Jens Schwanen told the Rheinische Post newspaper water levels at Germany's Kaub gauging station, a major bottleneck for Rhine navigation, were forecast to drop into single digits for the first time due to lack of rainfall.
Kaub lies south of the city of Koblenz at one of the shallowest sections on the Middle Rhine.
"Commercial shipping will no longer be able to transport goods in the region at such low water levels," he said. "The same goes for day trips and cruise shipping."
"In principle, the Rhine is then no longer navigable along its entire length and thus split in two," he added.
Schwanen said shipping would continue between the ports of Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Antwerp, the northern part of the German Rhine and the west German canal network, and farther south there would be traffic on tributaries including the Main, Moselle and Neckar rivers and the Main-Danube Canal.
This weekend, Germany's most populous state, North Rhine-Westphalia, as well as Lower Saxony, Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland relaxed trucking curbs to ease transport bottlenecks caused by low water levels on rivers including the Rhine.
Last Thursday, the country's inland navigation agency said low water levels on the river Rhine pose increasing problems and costs for freight shipping.
Inland navigation agency WSV said the navigable water depth at the chokepoint of Kaub near Koblenz was 19 cm on Thursday, below the previous lowest recorded level of 25 cm in 2018.
The river is about 1m deeper than the navigable depth.
Shallow water after this summer's heatwave and scarce rainfall means freight vessels are often only able to sail part-loaded, with extra surcharges increasing costs for cargo owners.
Loads must be spread among several vessels sailing partly loaded, creating unwelcome extra expense for German industry.
"Under the current extremely severe conditions, the cargo-carrying capacity of vessels is significantly restricted," said a spokesperson for German inland shipping company HGK Shipping.
"The vessels currently able to operate can transport only around 20 per cent of the tonnage that would normally be possible. The actual loading capacity varies depending on local water levels along the Rhine."
The Rhine is an important shipping route for commodities such as grains, minerals, ores, coal and oil products, including petrol.

Title: 30 years on Everest, 'Green Boots' set to be brought home
Article:
LADAKH, India: The remains of an Indian climber believed to have died on Mount Everest 30 years ago are set to be brought home to his family, the BBC reported.
A specialist Indian recovery team is preparing for a high-risk mission to retrieve the remains, believed to be those of Dorje Morup, 48, who died in a snowstorm while descending from the summit in May 1996.
The body, known as "Green Boots", was identified earlier this year. The nickname comes from the bright green Koflach mountaineering boots he was wearing when he died.
His remains have been preserved in ice at an altitude of about 8,500 metres.
Morup's wife, Konchak Yangskit, 75, said she and her family never gave up hope that he would one day return home.
Morup was among six climbers caught in a severe snowstorm while attempting to become the first Indian team to conquer Everest via the more challenging northern route from China.
The remains were initially believed to belong to Tsewang Paljor, another climber who died during the same expedition.
However, accounts from survivors and the location of the team's last radio contact led authorities to conclude they were likely Morup's.
The Indo-Tibetan border police appealed in June for a specialist high-altitude rescue team to retrieve the remains from the Tibetan side of Everest.
DNA testing will be carried out to confirm the identity. If confirmed as Morup, his remains will be returned to his family, who plan to hold a final farewell and burial ceremony in Leh, Ladakh.
Since 1996, Green Boots has served as a grim landmark for climbers using the northern route to Everest's summit. Some have even sheltered beside the remains during their ascent.
In 2006, climber Tshiring Jangbu Sherpa encountered the body while seeking shelter from strong winds, finding it almost completely covered by a thin layer of snow.

Title: MRCB, Teco team up on AI-ready modular data centres
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) has teamed up with Taiwan-based Teco Electric & Machinery Co Ltd to develop artificial intelligence (AI)-ready modular data centres (MDCs).
The two companies signed a memorandum of understanding to develop, deploy and operationally validate MDCs designed to support air- and liquid-cooled cabinet rack platforms.
MRCB said the MDCs will serve as a testbed to assess the technical and commercial viability of Teco's modular data centre technology, with the potential for similar developments across its landbank.
Under the partnership, MRCB will lease suitable land parcels with existing power supply allocations for the MDCs, while handling local authority submissions and regulatory approvals.
The companies will also explore opportunities to deploy MDCs through a design-and-build delivery model.
Teco, meanwhile, will provide modular data centre technology, specialised engineering solutions and operational management for the project.
MRCB group managing director Datuk Imran Salim said the collaboration would support the company's diversification into high-performance digital infrastructure while allowing it to scale up the use of its landbank.
"Expanding upon our previously announced intention to develop a 65-megawatt AI-ready facility designed for large-scale enterprise workloads, this modular data centre development demonstrates the versatility and our ability to scale up the utilisation of our landbank," he said.
He said integrating Teco's modular technology with MRCB's master development and engineering expertise would enable the group to serve a wider range of market demands.
The project is also expected to support MRCB's objective of generating recurring revenue and unlocking value from its landbank.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Contractor fined RM25,000 for failing to ensure construction site safety
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A construction company director was fined RM25,000 by the Sessions Court here today for failing to properly guard a floor opening at a construction site.
Judge Irwan Suainbon imposed the fine on C.Y.C. Management Sdn Bhd director Lo Chee Leong, 64, after considering the facts of the occupational safety and health case.
The court also ordered six months' imprisonment if he fails to pay the fine.
According to the charge, Lo, as the contractor responsible for construction works, failed to ensure that floor openings which could expose people to the risk of falling from height were adequately and properly guarded.
He committed the offence at C.Y.C. Management Sdn Bhd, Lot 3402 (former Lot 2756), Section 6, Jalan Lim Lean Teng here about 11.30am on Feb 20, last year.
He was charged under Regulation 19(3) of the Occupational Safety and Health (Construction Work) (Design and Management) Regulations 2024, under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, punishable under Regulation 19(6) of the same regulations.
The provision carries a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment for up to one year, or both, upon conviction.
In mitigation, Lo appealed for minimum fine and submitted photographs of the site showing remedial measures had been taken to address the offence.
However, Occupational Safety and Health Department (DOSH) prosecuting officer Khairul Nizam Mat Piah sought a deterrent sentence, stressing the need for contractors to take workplace safety and health requirements seriously.
The court subsequently imposed the RM25,000 fine as a deterrent, taking into account the importance of ensuring occupational safety and health compliance at construction sites.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sand unit price index rises 0.1 to 14.9pct nationwide in July
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The unit price index of sand increased in July 2026, ranging from 0.1 per cent to 14.9 per cent nationwide, compared to the previous month, said the Statistics Department.
In a statement today, the department said the highest increase in the price index for sand was recorded in Terengganu and Kelantan (14.9 per cent), followed by Kota Kinabalu, Sabah (4.1 per cent) and Penang, Kedah and Perlis (2.8 per cent), respectively.
"The unit price index of steel also edged up slightly in July 2026, ranging from 0.6 per cent to 0.9 per cent month-on-month (MoM).
"The highest increase in the price index for the material was recorded in Perak (0.9 per cent), followed by Tawau, Sabah (0.7 per cent), and Sandakan, Sabah (0.6 per cent)," it said.
Additionally, the department reported that the price index of cement registered an slight increase in July 2026,  ranging from 0.2 per cent to 0.8 per cent MoM across all areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
The highest increase in the price index for the material was recorded in Perak (0.8 per cent), followed by Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka, and Negri Sembilan (0.3 per cent), respectively, and Penang, Kedah and Perlis (0.2 per cent), respectively.
On a year-on-year basis, it said the unit price index for steel recorded an increase ranging from 0.5 per cent to 8.4 per cent involving most areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
According to the department, the highest increase in the unit price index for steel was observed in Perak (8.4 per cent), followed by Johor (6.3 per cent) and Pahang (4.8 per cent).
"The unit price index for cement also recorded increases ranging from 0.9 per cent to 7.5 per cent in July 2026 compared with the same month of the previous year across all areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
"The highest increase was recorded in Perak (7.5 per cent), followed by Kuching and Miri, Sarawak (7.2 per cent), respectively," said it.
Meanwhile, the departmetn said the average price per unit of steel, consisting of mild steel round bars and Mycon 60 high-tensile deformed bars, saw a slight decrease of 0.2 per cent MoM, with an average price of RM3,499.50 per tonne compared to RM3,507.10 per tonne in June 2026.
The average price of Ordinary Portland cement remained unchanged at an average price of RM25.70 per 50-kilogramme bag.
On the other hand, the Building Material Cost Index (BCI) with steel bars, by building category and region in Peninsular Malaysia for July 2026, rose by between 0.1per cent and 1.4 per cent MoM.
"The BCI with steel bars in Sabah recorded a slight decline, ranging from 0.2 to 0.5 per cent MoM for all building categories in July 2026, while BCI with steel bars in Sarawak saw an increase of 0.2 to 1.3 per cent MoM for all categories of buildings," it added.

Title: Malaysia must build talent fast to keep pace with AI, says Akmal
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping jobs and industries, making early talent development critical to Malaysia's economic ambitions, said Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
The Economy Minister said AI and other emerging technologies were changing the way businesses operate, requiring Malaysia to equip its young people with skills to remain relevant in a fast-evolving economy.
"Technology is moving so rapidly out there. We need to equip our children with the skills to adapt to technology, jobs and challenges that are constantly changing and enable them to remain relevant," he said.
Citing the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025, Akmal said 170 million new jobs were expected to be created globally by 2030, while 92 million jobs could be displaced by structural changes in the labour market.
He said 86 per cent of employers also expected AI and information-processing technologies to transform their business operations.
Akmal said Malaysia therefore needed to strengthen its talent pipeline to support the country's transition towards high-growth, high-value industries, particularly the semiconductor sector.
He said Penang was well positioned to pilot a more integrated science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) talent development model, given its established electrical and electronics, semiconductor and high-technology manufacturing ecosystem.
Penang recorded 7.3 per cent economic growth in 2025, exceeding the national growth rate of 5.2 per cent, while its manufacturing sector expanded 10 per cent, driven by the electrical and electronics and optical products industries.
The state's gross domestic product reached RM130.3 billion, while it accounted for 48.9 per cent of Malaysia's exports as of June this year, he said.
Akmal said the strong industrial ecosystem had already created high-value employment opportunities, but the challenge was ensuring local talent was ready to take advantage of them.
"Industry is already here and the opportunities are already here. The question is whether our students and the next generation are ready to seize these good opportunities?" he added.
He said Malaysia also needed to prepare 60,000 skilled engineers to support efforts to move further up the semiconductor value chain, including strengthening capabilities from back-end to front-end activities.
Akmal said the country should move beyond merely hosting manufacturing facilities towards developing Malaysian talent capable of creating higher-value products and technologies.
"We want to change from 'Made in Malaysia' to 'Made by Malaysia'. It is not merely about having factories here, but having our talent create higher value," he said.
He said STEM talent development must begin early, from primary and secondary education, before being strengthened through higher education, technical and vocational education and training, and industry training.
The Economy Ministry has agreed to allocate RM12.3 million over four years to support Penang's STEM blueprint, with the initiative targeting 100,000 students by 2030.
Akmal said the programme would connect schools, industry and students in a wider ecosystem, with the Penang model potentially being replicated in other states if successful.
He said industry players should also expose students directly to emerging technologies by bringing them to workplaces and having engineers visit schools.
"We want more from them. We want them to shape our future. We want them to provide leadership in technology," he said.
Akmal said Malaysia's long-term competitiveness depended on producing talent capable of driving innovation and strengthening the country's position in the global semiconductor supply chain.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's July palm oil stocks rose 3.32pct - MPOB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's July palm oil stocks rose 3.32 per cent from the previous month to 2.63 million tonnes, data from the industry regulator showed on Monday.
Crude palm oil production gained 9.41 per cent from June to 1.79 million tonnes, while palm oil exports surged 14.5 per cent to 1.39 million tonnes, the Malaysian Palm Oil Board said.
A Reuters survey had forecast inventories at 2.61 million tonnes, with output seen at 1.76 million tonnes and exports at 1.38 million tonnes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang grants PLB Engineering extension until Oct 18 for Jelutong landfill project
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government has granted PLB Engineering Bhd (PLBE) an extension until Oct 18 to complete outstanding requirements for its Jelutong landfill project.
State Local Government, Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the extension was approved by the state executive council at its meeting on Aug 5.
He said the extension was granted to allow the company to complete the remaining processes and fulfill all conditions and requirements set by the relevant technical agencies.
"The state government will continue to closely monitor the implementation of this project to ensure that all conditions and obligations are fully complied with by the developer, in line with technical and legal requirements and the public interest," he said in a statement today.
The extension covers PLBE's proposal for the safe closure of the Jelutong landfill, provision of a new disposal site for construction waste and marine clay, and development of the rehabilitated site.
H'ng said the decision took into account the agreed project planning, as well as the interests and requirements of all parties involved.
The project has
faced opposition
from the Protect Karpal Singh Drive Action Committee (ProtectKarpal), which has called on the state government to terminate the joint development agreement (JDA).
The residents' group had also urged Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow to honour his pledge that no further extension would be granted if PLBE failed to secure Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) approval by Feb 28.
ProtectKarpal claimed the deadline passed without EIA approval and alleged that the project had failed to secure approval on five occasions.
In June, the group also urged Chow to clarify whether another extension would be granted to PLBE after the Department of Environment rejected the project's EIA report.
SThe group has raised concerns over the proposed RM1 billion Jelutong landfill rehabilitation and coastal reclamation project off Karpal Singh Drive, including its potential impact on the Middle Bank Marine Sanctuary and potential environmental and public health risks associated with waste management activities.
The latest extension granted by the state government runs until Oct 18.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TH reforms yield results as investment, profit distribution improved – Economist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) reform efforts are beginning to show results as the institution's investment performance and profit distribution have improved, with the distribution rate increasing to 3.5 per cent for the financial year of 2025.
Putra Business School MBA Programme director Ahmed Razman Abdul Latiff said the development forms part of TH's reforms, including the implementation of the Royal Commission of Inquiry's (RCI) recommendations.
"Currently, TH has started to record an increase in return on investment, the highest number of depositors and also an increase in last year's profit distribution by 3.50 per cent, which is the highest in the last eight years.
"These are all indicators or undeniable evidence that TH has fully recovered and no money has been lost. RCI intends to caution, especially the current management of TH, to be prudent," he said during Bernama TV's programme "Apa Khabar Malaysia: RCI Tabung Haji -- Memelihara Amanah Pendeposit" aired today.
He said TH had implemented more than 75 per cent of the 25 RCI recommendations completed during TH's governance transformation and recovery phase.
Hence, he hoped that depositors do not need to worry about the status of their savings at TH following the RCI report on the institution.
"Depositors' savings in TH are definitely safe and secure. There is no need to panic as their savings are fully guaranteed by the government. The more we save, the more is guaranteed," he said.
In addition, Ahmed Razman said that, from an Islamic finance perspective, the management of TH depositors' funds must be based on shariah principles, transparency, and accountability, with the interests of depositors remaining a priority.
He said TH is a unique institution because it manages depositors' savings and invests the funds; its goal at its establishment was broader, which is to improve the economic status of Muslims so they could perform the hajj and have sufficient savings and assets to continue their lives afterwards.
Ahmed Razman opined that TH's fund management needs to be implemented under a strict process and in accordance with shariah principles, while ensuring that transparency and accountability are prioritised so that depositors understand how their funds are managed.
On July 29, the RCI on TH released a 211-page report on the investigation into the management and operations of the institution for the period 2014 to 2020.
A special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat will be held on Aug 11, 2026, to debate the report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 16-year-old boy admits to raping, sexually assaulting schoolgirl in library toilet
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 16-year-old student pleaded guilty at the Magistrate's Court today to raping and sexually assaulting a female schoolgirl in a library toilet
The accused entered the plea after the two charges were read before Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
He was charged with raping and sexually assaulting the 16-year-old girl at a library toilet at 1.30pm on May 7.
Each offence carries a maximum 20 years' imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
However, juvenile offenders may alternatively be subjected to a good behaviour bond, fined or sent to a Henry Gurney School.
The girl's mother lodged a police report on Aug 5 after being called to the school by a teacher, who informed her that her daughter had allegedly been raped by her boyfriend.
The report led to the accused's arrest.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shazleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer Haryanti Othman from the National Legal Aid Foundation.
The court allowed bail at RM3,000 and fixed Sept 30 for mention, statement of facts and sentencing pending a Welfare Department report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Intra-Asean trade must rise beyond 25pct, says Mohamad Hasan
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Asean must increase trade among its member states, which currently accounts for less than 25 per cent of the bloc's total trade, if the region is to fully realise its potential as one of the world's largest economies.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said strengthening intra-Asean trade was crucial, particularly as the region was on track to become the world's fourth-largest economy by 2030 based on its current trajectory.
"We want to see trade among Asean countries increase because, as of today, intra-Asean trade does not exceed 25 per cent.
"There is still much more that needs to be done to increase trade among Asean member states," he said during a press conference after opening the 59th Asean Day celebration at Wisma Putra here today.
Present were Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing and Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni.
Also present were New Straits Times deputy group editor Sharanjit Singh and Media Prima Television Networks deputy group editor (news and current affairs) Azhari Muhidin.
Mohamad said Asean was no longer focused primarily on political issues, but was increasingly placing emphasis on developing itself into a stronger and more influential economic bloc.
He said Asean's economic potential must be fully harnessed by strengthening trade links among member states, including through mechanisms that facilitate the movement of goods across borders.
"We are looking at mechanisms that can increase trade, including what we call the free movement of goods among Asean countries.
"This will further facilitate the trade that we want to increase among Asean member states," he said.
Mohamad said stronger intra-Asean trade was also important to ensure that the benefits of economic integration were shared more widely among member states.
He said Malaysia, during its Asean chairmanship last year, had introduced various initiatives and resolutions that laid the foundation for the continuation of the region's economic agenda.
He said the Philippines, as this year's Asean chair, was continuing proposals and resolutions adopted under the Kuala Lumpur Declaration and during Malaysia's chairmanship.
Mohamad said Malaysia would also continue to play an important role in ensuring that the Asean Community Vision 2045 was realised, following the trust placed in the country as the permanent shepherd of the vision.
He said one of Malaysia's priorities was to ensure that trade remained a key pillar in efforts to deepen Asean economic integration.
"With Malaysia entrusted as the permanent shepherd of the Asean Community Vision 2045, we want to ensure that our foundation, which is trade, can be further strengthened and advanced together," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sony, TSMC to spend US$6.3bil to jointly make image sensors, Nikkei says
Article:
TOKYO: Sony Group and Taiwan's TSMC plan to spend around one trillion yen (US$6.32 billion) to jointly make next-generation microchips used in image sensors, the Nikkei business daily said on Monday.
A joint venture owned about 60 per cent by Sony and 40 per cent by TSMC will start commercial production as early as 2029 in southern Japan's Kumamoto prefecture, the paper said.
The two tech giants said in May they planned to form a joint venture in Japan to develop and manufacture next-generation image sensors, combining Sony's sensor design expertise with TSMC's manufacturing and process technology strengths.
Sony and TSMC also said then that the partnership will explore opportunities in physical artificial intelligence applications such as automotive and robotics.
Sony is the world's largest maker of image sensors widely used in smartphones and autos, while TSMC is the world's largest contract chipmaker.
Sony declined to comment on the Nikkei report, while there was no immediate response from TSMC to Reuters' request for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JP Morgan raises S&P 500 year-end target to 8,000
Article:
NEW YORK: JP Morgan on Monday raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 to 8,000, citing strong corporate earnings and signs that AI investments by hyperscalers are poised to generate faster revenue growth.
The new target implies a roughly 3.12 per cent upside from the close of 7,757.64 points on Friday.

Title: Five remanded another seven days over businessman's murder in Batu Pahat
Article:
BATU Pahat: The remand of five men suspected of murdering a 39-year-old businessman, whose body was found wrapped in a net and floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, here last week, was extended.
The extension, granted by Magistrate Aimi Nawwar Mohamad Othman, takes effect tomorrow until Monday to allow police to continue questioning the suspects, aged between 26 and 40.
The five were previously remanded for seven days until today.
They are being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
The case came to light after residents found the
victim's body
floating in the river at about 11.30am on Aug 3.
Preliminary investigations found that the victim was allegedly strangled with a rope before his hands were bound with adhesive tape and his body wrapped in a net.
Police also found five stones on the body, believed to have been used to weigh it down and prevent it from resurfacing.
The discovery ended the mystery surrounding the disappearance of the businessman, who was reported missing from Mutiara Rini, Iskandar Puteri, on July 29.
The victim was identified by his next-of-kin based on the clothing and personal belongings found with the body.
Two of the five suspects have previous criminal and drug-related records.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Arul Kumar is new DAP Negri Sembilan chairman
Article:
SEREMBAN: Nilai assemblyman and National DAP vice-chairman J. Arul Kumar has been appointed as the new Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman, effective today.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the state committee unanimously selected Arul Kumar after he stepped down from the position, which he had held for 22 years since 2004.
"Arul Kumar's appointment is a very positive development and demonstrates that DAP is a multiracial party. We assess individuals based on their qualifications and ability to lead," he said.
Loke also expressed confidence in the new state committee, describing its members as experienced, united and accustomed to working together.
"Most importantly, we will continue serving every constituency we represent with dedication," he told a press conference after chairing the Negeri Sembilan DAP state committee meeting.
Loke said Arul Kumar, previously the Negeri Sembilan DAP vice-chairman, was appointed in accordance with the party constitution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget development proposals at final screening stage, says Akmal Nasir
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Economy Ministry is in the final stage of screening development proposals for the 2027 Budget, with submission to the Finance Ministry expected by mid-August.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the ministry was finalising its assessment before submitting recommendations for development allocations under the second rolling plan (RP2) of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).
"At the moment, at the Economy Ministry level, we have reached the final stage of budget screening before submitting our findings for development in 2027 to the Finance Ministry," he told newsmen here today when met after the launch of the STEM talent pilot project at Tech Dome.
Also present was Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
Akmal said the process involved several stages, beginning with the implementing ministries, before development allocations were coordinated and endorsed by the Economy Ministry.
He said the ministry was assessing new funding requirements as well as ongoing projects to ensure they remained aligned with the country's development priorities.
"For 2027 development, we are indeed looking towards strengthening the 13th Malaysia Plan," he added.
Akmal said RP2 would focus on addressing infrastructure and facility requirements, while strengthening the readiness of government agencies to accelerate the development of high-growth, high-value industries.
He said projects already approved under the first rolling plan (RP1) would also be taken into consideration when assessing priorities for the next phase.
On Penang's STEM development, Akmal said the ministry had agreed to allocate RM12.3 million over four years to support the state's STEM blueprint, which aims to train 100,000 students by 2030.
He said the initiative could serve as a pilot for a broader ecosystem-based approach to boosting interest in STEM and developing talent for high-value industries.
"Because of this, we see the approach as an ecosystem-wide effort to bring greater interest in STEM, which we can make a pilot project in Penang and, based on its success, introduce it in other states," he said.
Akmal said the initiative would also help prepare local talent for better-paying employment opportunities, particularly in the semiconductor and electrical and electronics sectors.
He said collaboration between the Federal Government, state authorities and industry players was crucial to ensuring the country's talent pipeline remained aligned with future economic needs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Roman wreck carrying hundreds of amphorae found off Sicily
Article:
ROME: Italian divers have discovered the 2,100-year-old wreck of a Roman ship off Sicily, piled high with hundreds of well-preserved amphorae, which were likely used to transport wine.
The wreck, dubbed by Italy's Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli as "one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years", was found some three miles off the coast of Mazara del Vallo.
Divers from the cultural heritage protection arm of Palermo's police said Saturday they had located the ship – thought to date to between the 2nd and 1st centuries BC – some 46 metres (150 feet) down, after a tip-off from fishermen.
Underwater fishermen Giacomo De Mola and Igor Bisulli described how they stumbled upon the wreck.
"Visibility wasn't the best... I got closer. And my heart stopped. Below me was a vast expanse of amphorae," De Mola said in an instagram post, along with video footage of the discovery.
The ship, reported in local media to be some 21 metres long and six metres wide, was mostly carrying Dressel 1A amphorae, which were tall and cylindrical, and mainly used for carrying wine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Decades on, Merdeka spirit still burns brightly among the elderly
Article:
IPOH: Do you still remember names such as Ali, Siti, Muthu, Jarjit Singh and Ah Meng that often appeared in our primary school textbooks once upon a time?
Those names, once so familiar to earlier generations, seem to bring back memories of friendship, unity and a spirit of togetherness in an independent nation.
That nostalgia was also felt by a group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, as this year's National Month celebrations took them back to their childhood days and, although decades have passed, memories of celebrating
Merdeka
(Independence) remain fresh in their minds.
The waving of the Jalur Gemilang and the sound of patriotic songs once again evoked memories of Merdeka celebrations among the group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, bringing back the nostalgia etched in their memories.
With great enthusiasm, the senior citizens sang Merdeka-themed songs together, made Jalur Gemilang flags and took part in a flag-assembling game during activities held at the community centre, demonstrating that their love for the country has never faded with age.
For 60-year-old Bhajan Singh, from Gunung Rapat, the activities organised by the community centre are not merely a way to fill his free time, but also an opportunity to reminisce about celebrating National Day during his childhood.
He said the opportunity to get together with his friends from various races also rekindled the spirit of unity that forms the basis of the country's harmony.
"Although I am getting older, my love for the country remains strong. My memories of celebrating the National Day for the first time are still fresh in my mind, although I was only a child at that time," he told Bernama recently.
Seventy-five-year-old Jaharah Hashim, from Manong, Kuala Kangsar, said the activities at the centre gave senior citizens the opportunity to forge friendships while putting their minds to the test.
"In the past, we would simply wave the Jalur Gemilang, but now it is more enjoyable because we get to get together with so many friends. Although I am a senior citizen, my enthusiasm for celebrating the National Day has never faded," she said.
For 64-year-old retired teacher P. Asokan, from Lahat here, the activities were truly meaningful as they brought together people from different ethnic backgrounds to appreciate the meaning of Merdeka.
"When I come here, I see Malays, Chinese and Indians all enthusiastically celebrating the National Day. This is the spirit that must continue to be nurtured so that we always appreciate the blessings of independence and national unity," he said.
Meanwhile, programme coordinator Nur Hayatulasna Mohamed Fishal said the National Day-themed programme was held for the first time at the community centre as an effort to foster the spirit of patriotism among senior citizens.
She said various activities had been organised, including singing patriotic songs, making Jalur Gemilang flags with Pos Malaysia and a flag-assembling game.
"Although it was held on a small scale, we hope this programme can inspire the spirit of Merdeka among the participants and strengthen ties within the community.
"Their age is advancing, and their strength may have diminished, but their gratitude for the blessings of independence and love for the country remain unwavering, proving that patriotism knows no age," she said.
'Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati' (Malaysia Madani: Shared Prosperity), which has been selected as the theme for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM 2026) celebrations, among other things, emphasises that the country's prosperity should be enjoyed fairly and comprehensively by everyone for the sake of shared harmony.
— BERNAMA

Title: 'Low-hanging fruit' projects can drive Sabah development, says Hajiji
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The implementation of "low-hanging fruit" projects could serve as a strategic catalyst for Sabah's development, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said issues raised during the recent state legislative assembly sitting included basic needs such as water and electricity supply, roads, flooding and drainage systems, as well as education.
"All these issues are related to the people's daily needs and some can be resolved through the implementation of 'low-hanging fruit' projects.
"While mega projects are important for long-term growth, these 'low-hanging fruit' projects can deliver immediate impact that the people and the government can feel within a shorter period," he said in a statement after chairing the State Development Action Council (MTPNg) meeting at Menara Kinabalu here.
Hajiji said the people had high expectations of enjoying the benefits of development without delay.
"I call on all ministries, departments and implementing agencies to strengthen their commitment further, enhance cooperation and improve strategic coordination.
"This is to ensure that every development project is implemented efficiently, systematically and according to the stipulated schedule."
Also present were Deputy Chief Ministers Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam and Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, state Cabinet ministers and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.

Title: Meta will soon face another high-stakes trial in US
Article:
WITH two convictions and nearly US$1 billion in damages already stacked up, Meta will face another trial starting this week about alleged harms to children in a case brought by four US states.
The federal trial, one of the most consequential among a myriad of legal proceedings targeting social networks in the United States, will begin Wednesday with jury selection at a federal court in Oakland, near San Francisco.
Opening statements are expected to start next week on Aug 18, with the trial lasting for roughly six weeks, followed by a verdict in early October.
The attorneys general of California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey allege the largest social media network in the world deliberately made Instagram and Facebook addictive for children.
And they are demanding a long list of restrictions on how Instagram and Facebook operate for minors, as well as up to US$1.4 trillion in penalties – nearly Meta's entire market cap which exceeded US$1.5 trillion last Friday.
CEO and founder Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses the prosecution plans to call to the stand; he also testified six months ago in a separate case that took place in a Los Angeles court.
While Zuckerberg has been known to spend an increasing amount of time living at his home in Hawaii, the company's headquarters in Menlo Park is about an hour's drive from the courthouse.
The Oakland trial is the culmination of a standoff that began in late 2021, when a former employee, Frances Haugen, leaked thousands of pages of internal research, dubbed the "Facebook Files," which showed that Meta had internally measured the potential harm Instagram was causing to some teenage girls, while publicly downplaying the impact.
The revelations triggered a joint investigation by dozens of states, which two years later resulted in a complaint filed by around 30 state attorneys general.
Four states will now attempt to prove their case together in Oakland.
TikTok, Snapchat and Google-owned YouTube have also been sued by thousands of families, school districts and prosecutors across the country in various local, state and federal lawsuits.
In a landmark trial that concluded in March, Meta and YouTube were convicted by a Los Angeles jury, which found both companies were responsible for a teenager's social media addiction.
That jury awarded the teenager US$6 million.
[[nid:1508008]]
On Thursday, a judge in New Mexico ordered Meta to implement product changes and pay more than half a billion dollars in damages to the state to fund the treatment and prevention of harms caused by Facebook and Instagram.
A jury in New Mexico previously ordered Meta to pay US$375 million after it found the company liable for endangering children by making them vulnerable to predators on its platforms, among other harms.
Meta has appealed, or intends to appeal, all of these decisions.
Meta is "confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts," Meta told AFP in a statement Thursday.
The company intends to argue that mental health is an industry-wide issue, and that some of the states' claims are protected by free speech laws.
In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for US$27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.
The four states in the Oakland trial accuse Meta of violating their consumer protection laws, in addition to a federal law that protects children's data, known as COPPA.
They allege that multiple features were designed to keep minors hooked, particularly infinite scrolling, excessive notifications and "like" counts.
It's a strategy that focuses on how apps are designed, not what is posted on them, essentially sidestepping the broad immunity internet sites enjoy in the US regarding content created by their users.
The staggering US$1.4 trillion in alleged damages comes from estimating the number of affected users in the four states.
However, the jury will have only an advisory role and Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers – who oversaw major trials between Apple and Epic Games, and Elon Musk and OpenAI – will decide on penalties, if Meta loses the case.
Parents of teenagers allegedly harmed by social networks might watch from inside the courtroom, as they did in Los Angeles, while the rest of the country can follow the proceedings from an audio-only livestream on YouTube.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Mohamad: Myanmar willing to repatriate 5,000 refugees by ship
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Myanmar has expressed its readiness to take back 5,000 refugees identified by Malaysia for repatriation, including transporting them home by ship, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
Mohamad said the proposal was being examined by the Home Ministry, while Wisma Putra would facilitate discussions between the two countries.
"When I met Myanmar's new foreign minister, they expressed their readiness to take back the 5,000 by ship.
"But the issue is the safety of these 5,000 people. When we send them back, will they be safe and what will happen to them? That must also be considered," he said after the 59th Asean Day celebration at Wisma Putra here today.
Mohamad said no timeframe had been fixed for the repatriation, but the process should be carried out as soon as possible once the necessary screening had been completed.
He clarified that the group comprised refugees from Myanmar of various ethnicities and was not limited to the Rohingya community.
"If they are from Myanmar, then they are Myanmar refugees. They are not solely Rohingya. There are various ethnic groups from Myanmar, including the Chin and Karen.
"It is best that we refer to them as Myanmar refugees," he said.
Mohamad said Malaysia regarded the refugee situation as a collective Asean responsibility, especially as ongoing instability in Myanmar continued to force people to flee the country.
"That is why Asean centrality in relation to the Myanmar issue is important. It is a common issue.
"We want the Five-Point Consensus to remain the core of Asean's mechanism in dealing with Myanmar, and we want the Myanmar government to fulfil the aspirations of Asean leaders because the consensus was agreed to by everyone, including Myanmar's leadership at the time," he said.
He said any proposed changes to the Five-Point Consensus must be brought back to Asean leaders for deliberation and approval.
Mohamad said Asean foreign ministers had also been tasked by regional leaders during their recent retreat in Cebu, the Philippines, to assess the latest developments in Myanmar and recommend the next steps, particularly in relation to the consensus.
He said the Five-Point Consensus itself was not difficult for Myanmar to implement if there was sufficient political will.
"If they want to do it, they can. The five points are not difficult — engage with the parties involved, stop violence against their own people and hold engagement with all sides in the conflict," he said.
Mohamad said Asean would continue pressing Myanmar to end violence against its people, which he said was crucial to preventing further refugee outflows.
"The important thing is that there must first be security within Myanmar itself so that those who are outside the country, not only in Malaysia but also in places such as Bangladesh, can return.
"There is no point sending them back only for them to flee the country again," he said.

Title: 'I regret not buying Haikal his favourite robot toy' - father mourns drowned son
Article:
PASIR GUDANG: A father was left grieving the loss of his 12-year-old son, who drowned with his friend at a dam here, with one regret weighing heavily on him — that he never got the chance to buy the boy his favourite robot toy.
Mohamad Khairudi Setapa, 42, said his son, Mohamad Haikal Ramzi, had become unusually quiet in recent weeks, a change from the cheerful boy who was close to his elder sister and younger brother.
"Haikal had become quiet lately. I am also sad that I did not get the chance to buy him his favourite robot toy," he said when met at the forensic department of Pasir Gudang Hospital today.
Haikal and his friend, Muhammad Adam Faris Arman, 11,
drowned at a dam
off Jalan Murai 2, Taman Scientex, here, after they were reported missing yesterday.
Khairudi said he last saw his second of three children at about noon yesterday before Haikal left home to play with his friend.
"Usually, he would return home before Maghrib. But when he did not come back yesterday, I immediately went to his friends' houses to look for him.
"I was later told that he had gone to the dam, which is about three kilometres from our home.
"When I arrived there, I saw my son's bicycle. We then lodged a report before firefighters arrived and began the search and rescue operation," he said.
His fears were later confirmed when rescuers found Haikal's body.
Khairudi said Haikal, a pupil of SK Kopok, had always been a cheerful child and was particularly close to his siblings.
"He was a cheerful boy and very close to his sister and younger brother. But I noticed that he had become quieter lately.
"I accept Allah's decree. My son was a trust from Allah for 12 years for me to care for.
"Insyallah, he will always be my son in this world and the hereafter," he said.
Haikal and Adam are scheduled to be buried at the Tanah Cahaya Masai Muslim burial grounds after Zohor prayers today.
Adam, a pupil of SK Kota Puteri 4, was also mourned by his family, who declined to be interviewed as they were still overcome with grief.
Earlier, Pasir Gudang Fire and Rescue station chief Senior Fire Officer I Haizrul Rahmad said both victims were found at 2.12am and 2.33am respectively.
He said the bodies were found at depths of about two and three metres from the dam bank respectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dewan Rakyat to debate Tabung Haji RCI report in special meeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Special Meeting of the Dewan Rakyat to discuss and deliberate on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report regarding Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will be held tomorrow.
Based on the schedule of the Special Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament on the Parliament portal, the Dewan Rakyat will convene for one day starting at 10am, and the session will be broadcast live on the Malaysian Parliament's YouTube platform and official media channels.
The special meeting is scheduled to begin with an explanation session by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, who will present an explanation regarding the RCI Report, followed by a question and debate session by Members of Parliament (MPs).
The debate session is then expected to be wrapped up by Zulkifli and the Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Last Wednesday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul agreed that the special parliamentary session on Tuesday would be held without breaks to provide sufficient time for MPs to discuss the TH RCI Report.
Fahmi said that at least 35 to 40 MPs have expressed their willingness to participate in the debate.
The 211-page RCI report on TH published on July 29 revealed various findings regarding the management and operational weaknesses of the institution during the period from 2014 to 2020.
Among the main findings of the RCI were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and profit distribution without considering the impact of depreciation and the decline in the fair value of investments.
According to the report, TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of a profit of RM3.4 billion as reported, if the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) were fully applied.
The findings indicate that TH's financial position at that time was at a critical level, with a deficit gap between assets and liabilities existing since 2014, as well as several issues related to investment depreciation.
The report also identified several factors contributing to TH's financial crisis, including high grant payments, creative accounting practices, the indecisiveness of the Auditor-General, the expansion of TH's vision as a pillar of the ummah's economy, and the increased burden of the Hajj Financial Assistance (Hafis).
The RCI report also found the existence of suspicious transactions and information concealment, and therefore recommended that a forensic audit be conducted, in addition to urging the authorities to take firm and immediate action on every police report and complaint regarding the management and operation issues of the institution during the period from 2014 to 2020.
On Saturday, the His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia decreed that the investigation into the RCI Report on TH should be carried out exhaustively..
His Majesty said that this step is important to ensure that every responsible party is subjected to appropriate action, in addition to ensuring that the same issue does not recur in the future.
– BERNAMA
