Title: Two company directors charged with failing to pay RM193,306 in sales tax
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Two directors of a caster wheel manufacturing company were charged in the Sessions Court here today with seven counts of failing to pay RM193,306.28 in sales tax and penalties.
The accused, Lim Hooi Cheng, 54, and Karen Loo, 40, appeared as summoned persons and pleaded not guilty to all charges after they were read before Sessions Court Judge Irwan Suainbon.
The charges involved seven taxable periods between January 2024 and February 2025, during which they allegedly failed to pay the sales tax within the stipulated period.
They were charged under Section 26(9) of the Sales Tax Act 2018 for violating Section 26(5) of the same Act.
Upon conviction, the offence carries a fine of up to RM50,000, imprisonment for up to three years, or both.
Customs Department prosecuting officer Mohamad Syafiq Abdul Aziz appeared for the prosecution, while Loo was represented by lawyer P. Gandhi.
Lim was unrepresented during the proceedings.
The court fixed Sept 10 for mention of the case and for Lim to appoint a lawyer.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alleged cartel boss Kinahan charged in Ireland
Article:
DUBLIN: An Irish court on Sunday charged alleged cartel boss Daniel Kinahan with directing a criminal organisation and remanded him in custody after his extradition from Dubai on a government jet.
The 49-year-old Irishman appeared in court after being flown back on Sunday evening from Dubai on the basis of an arrest warrant issued by Ireland.
He is alleged to be one of the leaders of a transnational group, known as the Kinahan Organised Crime Group (KOCG) or the Kinahan cartel.
The Irish government jet reportedly carrying Kinahan landed at Casement Aerodrome, a military air base west of Dublin at about 6.30pm (1730 GMT) as a helicopter circled overhead, an AFP video journalist saw.
Shortly afterwards a high-speed convoy of cars with blacked-out windows sped out of the gates, sirens blaring, watched by a crowd of people on the roadside.
Irish police later said in a statement they had arrested and charged a man in his late 40s over "serious organised crime offences" without naming Kinahan.
Irish police chief Justin Kelly said "this arrest shows our determination, along with our international policing partners including Dubai Police, to target transnational organised crime groups."
'HIGH-PROFILE' SUSPECT
Kinahan appeared shortly afterwards at the Special Criminal Court in Dublin, where he was charged with directing an organised crime organisation and remanded in custody until a hearing on October 5.
He was told the charge is that he directed the activities of a criminal organisation between October 2015 and April 2017.
Wearing a tracksuit bottom and a hoodie and glasses, Kinahan, flanked by plain-clothes police, appeared composed, reported the Irish Mirror.
The Special Criminal Court where Kinahan was taken is used for criminal cases involving terrorism and organised crime offences.
Trials there have three judges and no jury.
In a joint statement Sunday, UAE and Irish justice ministers called Kinahan "one of the most high-profile individuals sought for prosecution in connection with transnational organised crime."
'SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE'
Irish Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan said on X the extradition "sends a clear message that suspected perpetrators of serious and organised crime will find no safe haven from justice."
He hailed it as a "landmark of judicial cooperation with Dubai."
Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee called this "the culmination of years of determined work" by Irish police and successive governments.
Kinahan had lost a final appeal against extradition from the UAE, where he had been living openly for around a decade before his arrest.
He is be held in the high-security Portlaoise Prison in central Ireland, which houses some of the country's most notorious prisoners.
Kinahan moved to the UAE from Spain around 2016 after the murder of one of his associates and an attempt on his life at a boxing weigh-in at a Dublin hotel.
He also had ties to a now-defunct boxing management company that represented boxers including Tyson Fury and Carl Frampton.
Kinahan is the second person allegedly linked to the same criminal organisation to be extradited from Dubai.
Sean McGovern, described by a judge as "senior lieutenant in the cartel", was extradited after his arrest there in 2024.
In June, McGovern was sentenced to 24 years in prison in Ireland after pleading guilty to directing organised crime and attempted murder.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor to develop 'super app' for 12 local authorities
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor state government plans to develop an integrated application, or 'super app', that brings together the services and complaint channels of the state's 12 local authorities (PBT), State Local Government and Tourism Committee chairman Datuk Ng Suee Lim said.
Ng said the initiative aims to speed up and simplify public dealings by providing access to various services of local authorities through a single platform.
"I take note of the proposal. Recently, we have also received feedback from customers who said there are too many applications. Sometimes, they are confused about which application to use.
"I am confident that the approach we adopt can be continuously improved," he said in response to a supplementary question from Muhammad Hilman Idham (PN-Gombak Setia) on whether the state government planned to establish an integrated complaints platform at the state assembly sitting today.
Meanwhile, Ng said data security and confidentiality would also be prioritised to ensure users' details were not disclosed or misused, with regular monitoring to be carried out.
He said vendors involved in developing and operating the application would also be vetted to ensure only capable providers with good track records were selected.
Ng said counter services of local authorities would not be discontinued to assist those who were less digitally literate, particularly senior citizens and rural residents. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman escapes unhurt after car catches fire on Penang Bridge
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A Perodua Axia caught fire on the Penang Bridge early yesterday, damaging about 40 per cent of the vehicle, but no injuries were reported.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 3.07am about the incident at Km1.4 of the bridge, from the island towards Prai.
He said firefighters from the Prai Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 3.16am, about 20km from the station, and brought the fire under control at 3.20am.
"Firefighters conducted a size-up before carrying out control and extinguishing operations using the direct attack method.
"The fire was successfully extinguished at 3.26am, followed by overhaul operations before the case was handed over to the Fire Investigation Officer (FIO) for further action," he said today.
John said the fire involved the vehicle's engine compartment, while the cause of the fire had yet to be determined.
The vehicle was owned by a 29-year-old woman.
Nine firefighters, including a supervisor, were involved in the operation, supported by a fire and rescue tender and an emergency medical rescue services vehicle.
The operation ended at 4.28am, with police and Plus Malaysia Bhd also assisting at the scene.
No casualties were reported.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 8 teens charged with murder over fatal assault in Brisbane
Article:
SYDNEY: Eight teenagers have been charged with murder over the fatal assault of a 21-year-old man in Australia's Brisbane late in July, reported Xinhua.
The 21-year-old man died in hospital after he was found with significant head injuries by police who were called to a large disturbance involving a group of people in southern Brisbane in the early hours of July 26.
A police statement said that detectives on Sunday arrested four males, three aged 18 and a 17-year-old, and charged them with murder.
It comes after four others, two 19-year-olds and two 18-year-olds, were arrested and charged with murder on Thursday following extensive investigations into the incident.
Police initially said that officers at the scene on July 26 observed significant damage to vehicles and a residence.
The 21-year-old was located as people who were involved in the disturbance fled the scene. He was taken to hospital in a critical condition and died on Aug 1.
Police on Sunday thanked members of the community for significant assistance, cooperation and support provided to detectives throughout the investigation. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sanusi says Kedah may hold Penang ‘lease’ claim until Perikatan takes Putrajaya
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 10 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor reportedly said the state is considering delaying its claim for higher Penang “lease” payments, and instead wait for a Perikatan Nasional (PN) takeover of the federal government.
According to
The Star
, Sanusi said Putrajaya had yet to respond positively to Kedah’s demand despite the state pursuing a review of the payments for the past six years.
“If the federal government remains stubborn and refuses to pay or consider Kedah’s application, we will change the federal government,” he was quoted as saying.
“We are considering whether all these documents should be submitted now for discussion or later, after we become the federal government.”
Sanusi said Kedah had pursued a review for the past six years and had raised the matter with then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin during the PN administration, but the supporting documents were not ready for a formal submission at the time.
He said the state had since completed a study by historians and legal experts examining historical documents, agreements, payment records and the legal and constitutional basis of its claim, with the final report presented to state leaders on April 15 last year.
Kedah has said it is seeking RM300 million annually from the federal government, which has paid the state an annual RM10 million special contribution since 2018 in addition to the longstanding RM10,000 payment provided for under Article 167(7) of the Federal Constitution.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said last month that the matter fell under federal jurisdiction and that his state government had not received any legal correspondence from Kedah over the claim.

Title: Penang grants Jelutong landfill extension until Oct 2026, project faces scrutiny over EIA concerns
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Penang state government has granted PLB Engineering Berhad (PLBE) an extension of time (EOT) until October 18 for its proposed RM1 billion Jelutong landfill rehabilitation and development project.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the developer’s application for an extension was presented to the state executive council on August 5.
“Based on the presentation, the state government decided that an extension of time be granted until October 18, 2026,” he said in a statement today.
The project involves the proposed safe closure of the Jelutong landfill, the provision of a new site for the disposal of construction waste and marine clay, as well as development of the rehabilitated site.
H’ng said the extension was granted to allow PLBE to complete the remaining processes and fulfil conditions and requirements imposed by the relevant technical agencies.
He said the decision also took into account the agreed project plans and the interests and requirements of all parties involved.
“The state government will continue to closely monitor the implementation of this project to ensure that all conditions and obligations are fully complied with by the developer in accordance with technical and legal requirements and in the public interest,” he said.
The latest extension comes amid scrutiny over the proposed rehabilitation of the landfill and reclamation off Karpal Singh Drive, including questions over the project’s environmental impact assessment (EIA).
In June, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government had met with the Department of Environment (DoE) to better understand the considerations surrounding the EIA application for the project.
At the time, Chow said the DoE had accepted another EIA application from the developer and stressed that the state needed to go through the proper process before reaching a decision.
Non-governmental organisation Protect Karpal Singh Drive Action Committee, had previously questioned whether the developer under the Jelutong Landfill Joint Development Agreement was receiving “exceptional accommodations”.
The group had raised concerns over repeated extensions of time, revisions to payment structures and the scale of the proposed coastal reclamation.
It also questioned whether the financial restructuring and continued extensions were justified in light of previous EIA rejections and delays in the commencement of the project.

Title: High Court requests decision on venue for judicial review involving Negeri Sembilan Undang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The High Court has ordered counsel for three former Negeri Sembilan Undang and the incumbent Johol Undang to decide whether their judicial review will proceed here or Seremban, to avoid the risk of conflicting rulings on the same matter.
High Court judge Norliza Othman’s directive follows an earlier originating summons filed by the applicants at the Seremban High Court in May, which has yet to be heard,
The Edge
reported.
Counsel Mohd Khairul Azam Aziz, of Messrs Azam Aziz, was instructed to seek instructions from his clients on the matter. All parties are scheduled to return to court on Oct 7 to provide an update.
During the proceedings, the court also declined an oral application by Mohd Khairul for a gag order to prohibit public discussion of the case. The application was opposed by the Dewan Keadilan and Undang (DKU) and the Negeri Sembilan government, who argued that the proceedings involve matters of public interest.
The court has not yet ruled on a pending application by the DKU to intervene in the case; this decision remains deferred until Oct 7.
The applicants — Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashid, Datuk Abd Rahim Yasin, and Datuk Muhammed Abdullah — have named the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar (MB) and the state government as respondents.
In their judicial review application filed on July 17, the quartet is seeking a mandamus order to compel the MB to sign a proclamation document. This document seeks the removal of the present Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawer, and a further proclamation naming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar. The applicants are requesting that the MB sign the document within seven days of the court order.
Separately, the four Undang, along with Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman and Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid, filed an originating summons in the Seremban High Court in May. They are seeking a court order for the production of DKU minutes dated April 17, following the expulsion of Datuk Mubarak, a decision they are also challenging.
The DKU and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, have opposed this application, arguing that DKU matters are non-justiciable and outside the court's jurisdiction. Consequently, the court refused a stay over the decision to remove Datuk Mubarak.
In a related development, Seremban High Court judge Roz Mawar Rozain granted leave on July 8 for a committal hearing against the six applicants for the alleged violation of an ad-interim injunction.
The violation pertains to the holding of a DKU meeting and participation in the installation of Tunku Nadzaruddin on June 5. These committal proceedings are currently stayed pending an appeal at the Court of Appeal.
Senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan appeared for the Attorney General’s Chambers, while David Mathew appeared for the DKU.

Title: Akmal Nasrullah unveils RM12.3m Penang STEM programme, targeting 100,000 students by 2030
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The federal government will allocate RM12.3 million for a four-year STEM talent programme in Penang aimed at reaching 100,000 students by 2030.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the allocation will support the implementation of the Penang STEM Talent Blueprint, which was first introduced by Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow in 2024.
“We appreciate the efforts undertaken by Penang, so we agreed to collaborate with the target of training 100,000 students by 2030 as part of our efforts to promote interest in STEM,” he told a press conference after launching the STEM Talent Pilot Project here today.
He said the Economy Ministry had agreed to provide RM12.3 million over four years to implement the programme, which will expose students to science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) from an early age.
The pilot programme is a collaboration between the Economy Ministry and the Penang government to strengthen the talent pipeline needed by future industries.
Akmal said the programme will comprise four streams covering different levels of schooling, “Ignite: STEM Education” and “Ignite: MathQuest” for primary school students, “Embed: AI on Wheels” for lower secondary students, and “Embed: Technical Skill Learning” for upper secondary students.
The programmes were developed by Tech Dome Penang, Penang Math Platform, Penang Science Cluster and Penang STEM.
Akmal said Penang’s established industrial ecosystem made it an ideal location to test a model that could later be replicated elsewhere in the country.
“At the national level, we see that this whole-of-ecosystem approach to cultivating interest in STEM can be made a pilot project in Penang and, based on its success, subsequently introduced in other states,” he said.
He said the programme was not merely about increasing students’ interest in science and mathematics but about ensuring that local youths could participate in the higher-value economic opportunities being created around them.
Akmal said Penang already has a strong specialisation in the electrical and electronics (E&E), semiconductor and high-tech manufacturing sectors, making talent development increasingly important to sustain its industrial growth.
He said Penang’s economy grew by 7.3 per cent in 2025, compared with national gross domestic product growth of 5.2 per cent, while the state’s manufacturing sector expanded by 10 per cent.
Penang’s GDP reached RM130.3 billion, while the state accounted for 48.9 per cent of Malaysia’s total exports in June this year.
Akmal said technological advancement must be accompanied by efforts to ensure that local communities are not left behind.
“Talent development needs to begin earlier, from primary school to secondary school, and be strengthened through higher education, TVET and industrial training,” he said.
“When we talk about STEM at school level, it is not merely about mathematics or science. STEM shapes how our children think, how they solve problems, and subsequently builds their confidence and prepares them to go further,” he said.
The programme will also give particular attention to rural schools and lower-income communities, with students receiving hands-on exposure to emerging fields including artificial intelligence (AI), data science, robotics and digital technologies.
Akmal said 86 per cent of employers expect AI and information-processing technologies to change how businesses operate.
“Technology is moving so rapidly out there. We need to equip our children with the skills to adapt to technologies, jobs and challenges that are constantly changing, so that they can remain relevant,” he said.
Akmal said Malaysia also needs to develop 60,000 skilled engineers as the country seeks to move further up the semiconductor value chain from back-end activities towards higher-value front-end activities.
He said Malaysia’s next phase of industrial development should be about creating technology rather than merely manufacturing products developed elsewhere.
“Previously, we were proud when we successfully produced goods that were ‘made in Malaysia’. Now, we want to change that to ‘made by Malaysia’,” he said.
“It is not merely about putting factories here, but having our own talent create higher value,” he said.
He said the government ultimately wanted the students exposed to the programme to become more than workers equipped for future industries.
“We are no longer just clients or consumers. We are the innovators. We are the inventors that will change the landscape of technology even on the global stage,” he said.
Meanwhile, Chow thanked the Economy Ministry for backing the state’s STEM blueprint and providing the RM12.3 million allocation.
He said Penang had already implemented various STEM initiatives to support the state’s economic development, including programmes involving industry placements and new skills training.
“We have received good collaboration from industry, and many programmes involving the placement of students in industries are already taking place,” he said.
Chow said one of the aims was to equip students with practical skills from as early as Form Four, giving them the option of entering the workforce after completing their Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM).
“Part of our aspiration is that students who have completed their SPM can already start working because this programme prepares them from Form Four onwards,” he said.
Akmal also called on companies to go beyond supporting formal STEM modules by giving students first-hand exposure to workplaces and new technologies.
“If there is an opportunity, bring our children to your workplaces and show them what new technologies you are actually acquiring,” he said.
He added that the effectiveness of the Penang pilot will be evaluated and improved before it is considered for expansion to other states and economic sectors nationwide.

Title: Anthony Loke steps aside after 22 years, Arul Kumar appointed Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 10 — Nilai assemblyman and National DAP vice-chairman J. Arul Kumar has been appointed as the new Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman, effective today.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the state committee unanimously selected Arul Kumar after he stepped down from the position, which he had held for 22 years since 2004.
“Arul Kumar’s appointment is a very positive development and demonstrates that DAP is a multiracial party. We assess individuals based on their qualifications and ability to lead,” he said.
Loke also expressed confidence in the new state committee, describing its members as experienced, united and accustomed to working together.
“Most importantly, we will continue serving every constituency we represent with dedication,” he told a press conference after chairing the Negeri Sembilan DAP state committee meeting.
Loke said Arul Kumar, previously the Negeri Sembilan DAP vice-chairman, was appointed in accordance with the party constitution. — Bernama

Title: Budget screening nears completion, Economy Ministry to forward 2027 development proposals to MoF
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Economy Ministry expects to complete its screening of development expenditure proposals for 2027 by the middle of this month, before submitting its recommendations to the Finance Ministry (MoF), Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
He said the ministry is currently in the final stage of Budget screening as part of preparations for the Second Rolling Plan (RP2) under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).
“At the Economy Ministry, we have reached the final stage of Budget screening before we submit the proposals we have drawn up for development expenditure in 2027 to MoF.
“I expect that by the middle of this month, all processes at the Economy Ministry will be completed,” he told reporters today after launching the STEM talent pilot programme at Penang Tech Dome here.
Akmal said the Budget preparation process goes through several stages, including submissions from the respective implementing ministries.
Development expenditure proposals are subsequently submitted to the Economy Ministry for coordination and recommendation under RP2 for next year, he added.
He said the ministry is considering new allocations that need to be recommended while also reviewing the requirements of ongoing projects.
Asked about the main priorities for the upcoming Budget, Akmal said the government must ensure that the programmes and objectives outlined under the 13MP are supported by sufficient implementation capacity.
He said some of the initiatives had already been approved under the First Rolling Plan (RP1), while further requirements would be considered under RP2.
“For RP2, there are certainly several areas where I see a need, whether in terms of infrastructure or how government development expenditure can enhance or accelerate our move towards the high-growth, high-value industries that we have proposed,” he said.
Akmal said the government would also continue to take into account current requirements involving infrastructure, facilities and the preparedness of its agencies.
He said development spending for 2027 would ultimately be geared towards strengthening the implementation of the 13MP.
“For development expenditure in 2027, we are looking at strengthening the 13th Malaysia Plan,” he said.

Title: Two boys reported missing last night found drowned at Pasir Gudang dam after overnight search
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Aug 10 — The bodies of two primary schoolboys, who had been reported missing since last night, were recovered at a dam here by Fire and Rescue Department personnel early this morning.
The victims have been identified as Mohammad Haikal Ramzi, 12, and Muhd Adam Farish Arman, 11.
The two friends were believed to have drowned while playing at a dam in Jalan Murai 2 in Taman Scientex here yesterday evening.
“We were told the two children were earlier reported missing and their families became concerned when they did not return to their respective homes.
“Both victims were believed to have gone swimming in the dam based on the discovery of a bicycle and slippers belonging to one of the victims at the scene,” he said.
Pasir Gudang fire and rescue station operations commander Haizrul Rahmad said a water rescue team recovered Mohammad Haikal’s body at a depth of two metres and a distance of three metres from the dam’s edge at 2.12am.
He said Adam’s body was later found at a depth of two metres and a distance of 4.5 metres from the dam’s edge at 2.33am.
“The bodies of both victims were later handed over to the police for further action,” he said in a statement today.
Haizrul said the search and rescue operation, involving fire and rescue personnel from the Pasir Gudang and Skudai stations, ended at 3am.
He said a total of 19 personnel and six engines were earlier dispatched to the location at 11.49pm last night to conduct the search and rescue operation.

Title: Cashless for all: E-wallets now a national habit for Malaysians across generations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — E-wallets were long seen as a young person’s habit — something for students splitting bills or twenty-somethings ordering food delivery. New data from Ipsos Malaysia’s E-Wallet Landscape 2026 report suggests that story is out of date.
According to the survey of 1,029 Malaysians aged 18-74, conducted in April 2026, the fastest-growing group of e-wallet users last year was not the young.
It was Malaysians aged 35-44, whose usage jumped nine percentage points to 64 per cent, and those 45 and above, up four points to 44 per cent. By contrast, the 25-34 age bracket — traditionally assumed to be the core e-wallet demographic — stayed flat at 65 per cent, while 18-24 year-olds crept up just two points to 64 per cent.
Four years ago, e-wallets skewed heavily young. Today, usage across every adult age band sits within roughly 20 percentage points of each other, with the middle-aged group essentially level with Gen Z and millennials.
Ipsos points to where Malaysians are actually using their wallets as a clue. The strongest growth in usage occasions is not in online shopping — it is in everyday, offline spending: food and beverage outlets, toll and parking payments, and retail purchases.
“Malaysia has moved beyond digital payment adoption to digital payment dependence. For
businesses, being part of consumers' preferred payment ecosystem is increasingly critical to staying relevant,” Ipsos said in its report.
These are precisely the transactions a working, car-owning, family-supporting 40-something does daily — grabbing lunch, paying for parking at the office, buying groceries. As e-wallets embedded themselves into these routine errands, they stopped being a “digital-native” tool and became simply how bills get paid.
The report’s authors describe this directly: e-wallets are “no longer just a younger generation’s payment tool,” but an “everyday habit embraced by Malaysians across different life stages.”
What this means for consumers
For those in their 40s, 50s, or 60s who may still associate e-wallets with their children’s or grandchildren’s spending habits, the data suggests you have plenty of company adopting the technology — and there are practical reasons to keep up:
Convenience is now table stakes at toll booths and parking. With cashless lanes expanding, an e-wallet can shave real time off a commute.
Trust concerns are being addressed. Among the two leading platforms — Touch ‘n Go eWallet and MAE — safety and reliability scores sit at 77-82 per cent, suggesting the platforms have matured well past their early, glitch-prone days.
Wide acceptance removes the old excuse. Both leading wallets now report 76-81 per cent perceived acceptance among users, meaning “not enough places take it” is no longer the compelling argument it used to be.
A word of caution
Wider adoption among older Malaysians also raises the stakes on digital literacy and scam awareness.
As this demographic — often with larger account balances and less exposure to phishing tactics targeting younger digital natives — moves more of its daily spending onto phone-based apps, financial institutions and regulators may need to sharpen consumer education aimed specifically at midlife and older users, not just the young.
The bigger picture, though, is one of normalisation. What began as a convenience for the tech-savvy has become closer to a national habit, according to Ipsos, cutting across income groups, professions, and now, age.

Title: Transboundary haze worsens as nine Sarawak areas record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 10 — The number of areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze rose to nine this morning.
Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas were Kuching (161), Samarahan (161), Serian (179), Sri Aman (155), Sarikei (155), Sibu (158), Mukah (156), Bintulu (142) and Samalaju (141).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.
API data is updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Takiyuddin says PAS has no offers to join unity government, will await DAP’s decision
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — PAS secretary general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan declared the party has received no approaches or offers to join the unity government, stressing it will simply “wait and see” what happens when DAP decides its position on August 16.
“For August 16, we will wait and see. We have not received any approaches or offers to join the government. As of now, I can confirm there are none,” he told
Harian Metro
after attending the PAS annual convention committee meeting in Kota Bharu last night.
His comments come as DAP prepares to table a motion at its national convention, where nearly 4,000 delegates will determine whether the party remains in government until the end of the current parliamentary term.

Title: Melaka election is change for PKR to rebuild, says Adam Adli
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 10 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) views the Melaka state election as a “new platform” to rebuild its strength through a more mature political approach centred on ideas and policies that are clearly communicated to the people.
Acting Chairman of the Melaka PKR Leadership Council Adam Adli Abd Halim acknowledged that the party faces a major challenge in rebuilding public confidence after failing to win any state seats in the 15th Melaka state election in 2021.
“We need to prove to the public that the party remains acceptable and capable of producing elected representatives who can serve as the people’s voice in the Melaka State Legislative Assembly. We will begin this struggle without holding a single state seat.
“This challenge requires PKR to adopt a different approach from previous elections, including moving away from patronage-based politics towards a more mature political style,” he told Bernama.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
However, the Melaka State Executive Council (Exco) lineup also includes PH assemblymen, reflecting a Unity Government arrangement similar to that at the federal level.
Adam Adli, who is also a PKR Central Leadership Council (MPP) member, said PH would enter the state election with humility, seeking to establish itself as a coalition that remained close to the people and responsive to the needs of a multiracial society.
“We do not wish to label the public based on their various political leanings. Instead, we respect the maturity of voters in making their own assessments based on the proposals put forward,” he said.
The Hang Tuah Jaya Member of Parliament said PKR must continue to understand and address the needs of all segments of society, particularly issues involving the cost of living, youth, education, home ownership, wages and mental health.
“What we need to do is offer ideas, principles and policies that can benefit the people. This approach aligns with the ‘Justice for All’ concept, which aims to ensure that the party serves as a platform for all the Melaka people, regardless of their background,” he said.
Adam Adli, who is also Deputy Higher Education Minister, said a party’s success should not be measured solely by political dominance, but by the extent to which its ideas and policies benefit the community.
The mandate of the Melaka state government expires on December 31.
On the 2026 PKR National Congress, Adam Adli said it would focus on strengthening the party ahead of the state election.
Melaka will host the congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh from August 13 to 16, with Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim scheduled to officiate the event on August 15. — Bernama

Title: Zahid congratulates Malaysian men’s doubles pairs after Korea Masters one-two
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has congratulated men’s doubles pairs Tee Kai Wun-Yap Roy King and Soh Wooi Yik-Man Wei Chong for emerging as champions and runners-up, respectively, in the 2026 Korea Masters Badminton Championships yesterday.
Ahmad Zahid hopes their success will be just the right tonic to spur them to continue to bring glory to Malaysia on the international stage.
“Our two new pairs put up a thrilling and closely-fought match.
“Congratulations and thank you to everyone involved for your efforts and commitment,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Kai Wun-Roy King emerged champions in their Korea Masters debut at the Yi Sun-sin Gymnasium in Asan with a 21-13, 21-18 win over compatriots Wooi Yik-Wei Chong in 31 minutes.
This is the second time Malaysia has won the Korea Masters title, with Wooi Yik partnering Aaron Chia to lift the men’s doubles crown in 2024. — Bernama

Title: Parliament to debate Tabung Haji RCI report in special sitting tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — A Special Meeting of the Dewan Rakyat to discuss and deliberate on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report regarding the Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will be held tomorrow.
Based on the schedule of the Special Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament on the Parliament portal, the Dewan Rakyat will convene for one day starting at 10am, and the session will be broadcast live on the Malaysian Parliament's YouTube platform and official media channels.
The special meeting is scheduled to begin with an explanation session by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr. Zulkifli Hasan, who will present an explanation regarding the RCI Report, followed by a question and debate session by Members of Parliament (MPs).
The debate session is then expected to be wrapped up by Zulkifli and the Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Last Wednesday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul agreed that the special parliamentary session tomorrow would be held without breaks to provide sufficient time for MPs to discuss the TH RCI Report.
Fahmi said that at least 35 to 40 MPs have expressed their willingness to participate in the debate.
The 211-page RCI report on TH published on July 29 revealed various findings regarding the management and operational weaknesses of the institution during the period from 2014 to 2020.
Among the main findings of the RCI were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and profit distribution without considering the impact of depreciation and the decline in the fair value of investments.
According to the report, TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of a profit of RM3.4 billion as reported, if the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) were fully applied.
The findings indicate that TH's financial position at that time was at a critical level, with a deficit gap between assets and liabilities existing since 2014, as well as several issues related to investment depreciation.
The report also identified several factors contributing to TH's financial crisis, including high grant payments, creative accounting practices, the indecisiveness of the Auditor-General, the expansion of TH's vision as a pillar of the ummah's economy, and the increased burden of the Hajj Financial Assistance (HAFIS).
The RCI report also found the existence of suspicious transactions and information concealment, and therefore recommended that a forensic audit be conducted, in addition to urging the authorities to take firm and immediate action on every police report and complaint regarding the management and operation issues of the institution during the period from 2014 to 2020.
On Saturday, the His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia decreed that the investigation into the RCI Report on TH should be carried out exhaustively..
His Majesty said that this step is important to ensure that every responsible party is subjected to appropriate action, in addition to ensuring that the same issue does not recur in the future. — Bernama

Title: Immigration Dept arrests Pakistani man over alleged use of official logo, warning lights on vehicle
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 10 — The Immigration Department detained a Pakistani man who is believed to have used the department's official logo and warning lights on a vehicle, less than 24 hours after a video of the incident went viral on social media.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the man was detained in a special operation conducted at 4.30pm yesterday at PV3 Platinum Hill Condominium, Setapak, following intelligence gathered from the viral video showing a vehicle bearing the Immigration Department logo being used by a foreign national.
He said an inspection at the premises also led to the detention of an Indonesian woman who was found to have overstayed in the country, as well as the discovery of two Indonesian passports believed to belong to other individuals, which were in the man’s possession.
“Preliminary investigations into the individual featured in the viral video found that the video was recorded in April 2025 and was only uploaded as a WhatsApp status by the individual's wife on August 7. The individual's wife is in Indonesia, and the video was uploaded while she was there,” he said in a statement here today.
Zakaria said the Pakistani man was detained for allegedly committing offences under Section 12(1)(f) of the Passports Act 1966 and the Immigration Act 1959/63, while the Indonesian woman was detained under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Zakaria said following the arrests, the operation team traced a Toyota Hilux, believed to be the vehicle featured in the viral video, to a car wash premises on Jalan Kuching, Kuala Lumpur.
He said the vehicle’s actual owner, also a Pakistani national, was arrested along with eight other foreign workers - four Bangladeshis, three Pakistanis and an Indian.
The vehicle owner is being investigated under Section 55B of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while the eight workers are suspected of offences under Section 6(1)(c) of the same law for not possessing valid travel documents.
Zakaria said preliminary investigations found that the video was recorded in April 2025 before being uploaded as a WhatsApp status by the man’s wife on August 7 while she was in Indonesia.
He said the vehicle owner admitted installing the logo and directional warning lights for personal use, without any official purpose, and claimed he was unaware that doing so was an offence. He also claimed that the logo and lights had been removed before the video went viral.
All those detained, together with the vehicle featured in the video, were taken to the Immigration office for further action and investigation. — Bernama

Title: ‘Taking too long’: Man arrested after allegedly brandishing meat cleaver at delivery rider at Terengganu petrol station
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — Police arrested a man who allegedly acted aggressively and brandished a meat cleaver at a p-hailing worker at a petrol station on Jalan Pasir Panjang here yesterday afternoon.
Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 55-year-old suspect was arrested at about 10pm last night at his home in Kampung Nibung here.
He said investigations found that the incident was believed to have stemmed from the suspect’s dissatisfaction, as he claimed the victim had taken too long to refuel.
“At about 4.30pm, while the 26-year-old victim was refuelling his motorcycle, the suspect arrived on a Honda Wave motorcycle. The suspect suddenly shouted at and scolded the victim for allegedly taking too long to refuel, but the victim ignored him.
“The enraged suspect then took a meat cleaver from his motorcycle and brandished it at the victim. Fearing for his safety, the victim fled before lodging a police report,” he said in a statement today.
Azli said a urine test found that the suspect tested positive for methamphetamine and that he had 15 previous criminal records involving drugs, theft and assault with a dangerous weapon.
He said the suspect had been remanded for four days from today until August 13 to facilitate investigations under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation.
Earlier, a 23-second video went viral on social media showing a man brandishing a knife at a p-hailing worker while the victim was refuelling at a petrol station. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu police call for restraint as residents vent fury after foreigner crime case fuels tensions
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — Police have issued a stern warning to the public not to take the law into their own hands following the arrest of three Rohingya men suspected of sexually assaulting a woman with intellectual disabilities in Kampung Besut, Kemaman.
According to
Sinar Harian
, Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said any excessive action could disrupt public order and jeopardise the ongoing investigation.
“Leave all investigative matters and action entirely to the authorities,” he said in a statement last night.
The reminder came after local residents gathered at the Flat Kampung Enjin Gergaji in Chukai, Kemaman, to voice dissatisfaction over crimes involving foreigners in the area.
However, Mohd Khairi confirmed the assembly dispersed peacefully following police engagement and explanations.
Bernama reported yesterday that three Myanmar refugees aged 19 to 28 were arrested in Kemaman over the alleged sexual assault of a 23-year-old intellectually disabled woman.
Police confirmed the suspects have been remanded until August 12 as investigations continue to identify others possibly involved.

Title: Maintenance worker drowns after suspected fall into water tank at Kuala Langat power plant
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 10 — A contract worker drowned after he was believed to have fallen into a five-metre-deep water tank while carrying out maintenance work at the cooling tower of the Kuala Langat Power Plant in Kuala Langat here yesterday.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department was informed of the incident at about 7.29pm before personnel were deployed to the scene.
He said the body of the 34-year-old local man was found at about 4am today after a search operation was conducted in two pools at the power plant.
“The victim was carrying out maintenance work with a colleague to replace wood at the cooling tower before his colleague left to get more wood. When the colleague returned to the location 15 minutes later, he found that the victim was no longer there.
“Initially, the colleague thought the victim might have gone to the washroom, but became suspicious that he may have fallen after he failed to return. The colleague then informed the supervisor, who conducted a roll call and found that the victim was missing,” he said in a statement.
He said the case had been handed over to police for further action, while the operation involving personnel from Banting Fire and Rescue Station (BBP), Port Klang BBP and KLIA BBP ended at 5.05am today. — Bernama

Title: Anwar undergoing medical checks, PMO confirms two‑day specialist observation period
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is undergoing medical examinations and procedures prescribed by a team of specialist doctors, his office confirmed today.
Senior press secretary Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said Anwar is expected to remain under observation for two days.
“We pray that all examinations and procedures will proceed smoothly, and that the Prime Minister will be granted lasting good health to resume his duties as soon as possible, Insya Allah,” he said in a statement.
The Prime Minister’s office did not disclose further details of the procedures.

Title: Nadi offers cheaper school uniforms for families, says education minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Nadi School Uniform initiative not only helps families acquire school supplies at more affordable prices, but also opens up opportunities for alumni of the Nadi Sewing Skills programme to generate income through the skills they have learned.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek stated that this initiative originated from the Nadi Mahir Jahit programme provided under the National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi), which gives participants -consisting of housewives and single mothers - the opportunity to learn sewing skills before utilising those skills to generate family income.
“Over 2,000 participants have joined the Nadi Mahir Jahit programme, and it is now entering its fourth intake. It is from this programme that the Nadi School Uniform initiative was born.
“Alumni who already possess these skills are given the opportunity to produce school attire to be sold at more affordable prices to the community. This is truly an initiative that I support,” she said via a Facebook post yesterday.
Through its Lifelong Learning pillar, Nadi provides a platform for underprivileged and marginalised groups to access education and skills training, covering Nadi TINYTECHIE, NURTURE EKELAS Students, Nadi E-Sports, Nadi Rakyat Tuition, Nadi Cybersecurity, Nadi Skills (Sewing, Cooking, Gadget Repair, Photo/Video, Smart Agriculture, ICT Literacy), and the Nadi AI Programme.
Fadhlina said that for families in need, Nadi also provides an option to make instalment payments for the purchase of school uniform without imposing any interest or additional charges.
She noted that this facility is neither a loan nor a “Pay Later” scheme, but rather an option to help parents manage their expenses, especially when they need to prepare school supplies for multiple children simultaneously.
Elaborating further, Fadhlina said the greatest value of this initiative lies not merely in a way to buy a school uniform, but in the opportunities created when a person is given skills and the space to use them.
“A woman learns to sew. Her skill becomes a source of income. Her handiwork, in turn, helps other families save money.
“I believe a good programme does not just provide assistance for yesterday. It provides skills so that a person has more choices for today. One skill. Two families benefit,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Hajiji: Sabah will use RM1.5b federal special grant for infrastructure and welfare
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 10 — All revenue received by Sabah from the Federal Government will be channelled back to the people through various forms of incentives, assistance and development, says Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the increase in the interim special grant payment to RM1.5 billion from this year would be fully utilised to build more paved roads and concrete bridges as well as improve water and electricity supply throughout the state.
“We welcome Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s decision to increase the interim payment, and we will use the proceeds for development and people’s welfare agendas such as the construction of more Rumah Mesra Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) units and the Sentuhan Kasih Rakyat (SYUKUR) programme.
“Whatever we receive from the Federal Government will be returned to the people in various forms of incentives and assistance,” he said in his speech at the 32nd anniversary celebration of the United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko) and opening of the 17th Upko Triennial Delegates Conference here yesterday.
The Sabah state government was previously reported to have received RM600 million of the RM1.5 billion interim special grant payment disbursed by the Federal Government on June 12.
Meanwhile, Hajiji said the state government continued to focus on financial performance and increasing revenue collection, with annual collections maintained at RM7 billion since 2022 and expected to increase to RM8 billion this year.
He said Sabah’s economic resilience continued to be strengthened despite various domestic and global challenges, making the state a strategic investment destination. — Bernama

Title: Police: Four masked suspects break into Sungai Buloh home, make off with RM35,000 worth of valuables
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The police are actively conducting an investigation into a burglary case suspected to have been carried out by four masked suspects at a woman's residence in Sungai Buloh, Selangor, resulting in an estimated loss of RM35,000.
Sungai Buloh district police chief Supt Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said the report regarding the incident was received by the police yesterday.
“The incident has resulted in the loss of jewellery and the disappearance of several important documents,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Mohd Hafiz said that members of the public who have information regarding the incident are requested to contact the investigating officer, Sergeant Shamie Yusop, at 013-6463069 or the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters at 03-61561222 to assist with the investigation.
It is said that the case is being investigated under Section 457 of the Penal Code.
Earlier, a video went viral on social media showing a woman's house in disarray after it was believed to have been broken into, and reported missing was cash, mobile phones, jewellery and passports. — Bernama

Title: Sabah to acquire 30pc stake in two new oil and gas fields, says Hajiji
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 10 — The Sabah government will acquire a 30 per cent stake in two new oil and gas fields on the state's east coast, said Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the state government was also finalising the acquisition of 40 per cent equity in the floating liquefied natural gas facility project in Sabah.
“The agreement for this partnership will be signed soon. The government will also develop new industrial parks, including in Kota Belud and a blue economy hub in Kudat to boost investment in the state further and increase domestic economic chain activities,” he said at the 32nd anniversary of the United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko) and the opening of Upko’s 17th Triennial Conference here yesterday.
Hajiji, who is also Gabungan Rakyat Sabah chairman, said the development was part of the state government's efforts to strengthen Sabah's participation in the oil and gas industry through a strategic collaboration with Petronas under the Commercial Collaborative Agreement.
He said the collaboration had increased the state government's equity holding in the exploration and development of Sabah’s oil and gas industry. Additionally, it has opened up space for local companies to be involved in the industry’s development.
Hajiji also said that the state government continues to focus on strengthening financial performance and increasing state revenue collection as an important foundation in driving Sabah's development.
He said since 2022, the state government had managed to maintain revenue collection annually at the RM7 billion level. He expects state revenue collection to increase to RM8 billion this year.
“In 2025 alone, RM7.6 billion in investment value in the manufacturing sector was recorded, almost 208 per cent against 2024,” he said.
This achievement was also supported by the state's economic resilience in facing various domestic and global challenges, thus strengthening Sabah's position as a strategic investment destination. — Bernama

Title: Lim Lip Eng posts RM5,000 bounty after woman set alight in brutal Kepong petrol attack
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng has announced a RM5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of the suspect who doused a woman with fuel and set her alight in a brutal attack at Taman Pusat Kepong yesterday.
Lim described the assault as “an act of shocking cruelty” and urged police to hunt down the attacker swiftly.
“The person responsible must be found, arrested and made to face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement today.
He added that the cash reward is being offered for credible information that directly results in the suspect’s arrest, and warned the public not to approach or confront the attacker themselves.
Members of the public with details are urged to contact investigating officer Insp Muhammad Amri Firdaus Jusoh at 010 9198209, the Sentul district police headquarters at 03 40482222, or the nearest police station immediately.

Title: Number forecast operator doused in petrol and set ablaze while working in Kepong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Police have launched a special operation to track down a man who doused an elderly woman with a substance believed to be petrol before setting her on fire at the premises of a number forecast operator in Taman Pusat Kepong here yesterday morning.
Acting Sentul district police chief Supt Jasni Zolpa said the victim, 62, who worked as counter staff at the number forecast operator was attacked by the unknown suspect at 8pm
“Preliminary investigations revealed the victim did not have any enemies nor received any previous threats. The motive of the incident is being investigated,” he said in a statement yesterday, adding that the victim suffered about 50 per cent burns to her body and was rushed to Kuala Lumpur Hospital, where she is reported to be in stable but critical condition.
The Kuala Lumpur contingent police headquarters’ forensics team has also conducted further investigation at the scene of the crime and taken several samples of related items and deoxyribonucleic acid to assist investigations, he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code.
He urged those with information on the incident to contact investigating officer, Insp Muhammad Amri Firdaus Jusoh at 010-9198209, the Sentul district police headquarters operations room at 03-40482222 or the nearest police station.
In a separate case, Cheras district police chief ACP Mohd Rosdi Daud said a man, in his 20s, was injured in a scuffle outside Kuala Lumpur Football Stadium, Cheras last night after the end of the Hyundai Asean Cup match between Malaysia and the Philippines, adding that investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the incident.
Meanwhile, Kajang district police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said police are looking for witnesses of a crash that killed a motorcyclist, 35, who had lost control while driving in the left lane and fell into the middle lane and was hit by an unknown vehicle that was unable to avoid him at Kilometre 301.4 of the Kuala Lumpur bound Kuala Lumpur-Seremban (PLUS) Highway Saturday.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: If police stop you in Malaysia, here's what you should know
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — It happens more often than many people realise.
Maybe you’re pulled over at a roadblock. Maybe police stop you during an operation at a shopping mall or perhaps an officer approaches you on the street asking a few questions.
Or you maybe one of the rare ones who’ve had a knock on your door.
Do you have to answer everything? Can they search your phone? What if they ask you to follow them to the police station?
Then there’s the famous line we’ve all heard in countless Hollywood movies:
“I want my lawyer!” Does that actually work in Malaysia?
We’ve all seen the scenes.
A suspect is arrested, turns to the officer and declares:
“I want my lawyer.”
Questioning stops. A lawyer appears moments later.
In Malaysia, it doesn’t quite happen like that.
If you’ve been arrested, you have the right to consult a lawyer and to contact a family member or trusted friend.
Police should generally give you a reasonable opportunity to speak to your lawyer, although there are limited circumstances where they may delay this if immediate questioning is necessary for the investigation.
You should also tell your family or lawyer where you were arrested, why you were arrested and which police station you’re being taken to.
However before any of that happens, most encounters with police start much more simply.
Can police check your phone?
For many Malaysians, this is probably the first question that comes to mind.
The Malaysian Bar’s latest Red Book says police may inspect your mobile phone if they have a lawful reason to do so, such as when they reasonably suspect you’ve committed an offence, you’re being investigated, or you’ve been arrested.
If an officer asks to inspect your phone, don’t panic—but don’t be afraid to ask questions either.
Politely ask why your phone is being inspected and whether you’re being investigated or suspected of committing an offence.
Understanding why police are exercising that power can help you better understand your rights throughout the interaction.
A police officer stops you. What’s the first thing you should do?
First, stay calm.
If the officer is in uniform, make a mental note of their name and identification number. If they’re using a patrol car or motorcycle, note the vehicle registration number if you can.
If they’re not in uniform, politely ask to see their police authority card.
The colour tells you what authority they have:
Blue — Inspector and above.
Yellow — Officers below the rank of Inspector.
White — Reserve police.
Red — Suspended police officer with no police powers.
If possible, remember the officer’s name and identification number before the conversation continues.
Before answering questions, ask one yourself
People often assume that if police are questioning them, they’re already under arrest.
That’s not necessarily true.
Instead, politely ask:
“Am I under arrest?”
It might be the most important question you ask.
If the answer is no, you’re generally free to leave and do not have to accompany the police to a station simply because they ask.
If you’re told yes, or if you are handcuffed or prevented from leaving, you’re considered under arrest.
What information must you actually provide?
If you’ve simply been stopped by police, you’re generally only required to provide your personal particulars: Your name; NRIC number; and address.
Beyond that, your rights depend on the circumstances.
The guide also makes clear that police cannot arrest someone simply because they want that person to give a witness statement.
If you’re under arrest, ask these two questions
If police tell you you’re under arrest, don’t argue or physically resist.
Instead, ask:
“Why am I under arrest?”
Police should inform you why you’re being arrested.
Then ask:
“Which police station are you taking me to?”
Knowing where you’re being taken allows you to inform your lawyer or family member as soon as you’re able.
Can police search your car?
Yes, they can.
The updated Red Book explains that police have powers to stop and search vehicles in certain circumstances.
If your vehicle is being searched, remain cooperative but ask why the search is being conducted and whether you’re being investigated or suspected of committing an offence.
As with any interaction, note the officer’s name, rank and, if possible, the police vehicle’s registration number.
Can they search your pockets or bag?
Police may conduct searches during certain operations, but there’s a practical tip many people don’t know.
Instead of allowing officers to reach into your pockets or bag themselves, remove the contents yourself one item at a time, identify each item aloud and then turn your pockets or bag inside out.
If you’re a woman, any body search must be conducted by a female officer.
Strip searches aren’t automatic
Television often gives the impression that every arrest ends with a strip search.
It doesn’t.
The Red Book explains there are different types of body searches, ranging from a simple pat-down to strip, intimate and intrusive searches.
The more invasive the search, the higher the level of authorisation required.
How long can police keep you?
Police may generally detain someone for up to 24 hours while investigations are carried out.
If investigators need more time, they must bring you before a magistrate to apply for a remand order.
The magistrate isn’t obliged to grant the full period requested and may refuse the application or approve a shorter remand instead.
If you appear before a magistrate, tell the court if you’ve been denied access to a lawyer, require medical treatment or have been mistreated while in custody.
Before you sign anything… slow down
Whether it’s a witness statement or another document, don’t rush.
Read every page carefully.
Make sure it accurately reflects what you said.
If something is wrong, ask for it to be corrected before signing, and sign immediately below the last sentence so nothing can be added afterwards.
The bottom line
Most encounters with police end without incident.
Knowing your rights isn’t about refusing to cooperate or making an officer’s job harder. It’s about understanding what police can legally do, what you’re legally required to do, and asking the right questions if you’re ever stopped, questioned or arrested.

which explains the rights and responsibilities of the public during interactions with police.

Title: Pulau Tuba’s authentic village life pitched as Langkawi’s next big tourism secret
Article:
LANGKAWI, Aug 10 — Pulau Tuba has the potential to attract more domestic and international tourists with its authentic traditional village atmosphere and unique cultural experiences, said Kedah Tourism, Culture and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Salleh Saidin.
He said despite Langkawi recording more than three million tourist arrivals, visitor numbers to Pulau Tuba remained relatively low, highlighting the island’s untapped potential as a “hidden gem”.
“Tourist arrivals in Langkawi reach the millions, yet only a small number visit Pulau Tuba. This shows the island has tremendous potential that has yet to be fully developed.
“It offers a sense of tranquillity and an atmosphere that is difficult to find elsewhere. The local community continues to preserve its heritage and traditional cultural values, complemented by an authentic village landscape, including buffaloes roaming freely,” he told reporters.
Mohd Salleh said visitors could also sample unique local seafood delicacies such as bronok (sea cucumber) and siput gayam, a type of shellfish associated with the island.
“Tourists today are no longer simply looking for luxurious buildings and facilities, they are seeking unique experiences. I am confident that Pulau Tuba has the potential to become a premier tourism destination, and we will focus on promoting its unique attractions to international visitors.
“The state government recognises Pulau Tuba’s special appeal, so we will not neglect it. Greater focus and attention will be given to the island,” he said.
He added that various programmes and events were being organised to attract visitors to Pulau Tuba, which would help boost the local tourism sector and generate economic benefits for the community.
Meanwhile, 31 media practitioners from Kedah were given the opportunity to experience the island’s unique lifestyle, culture, traditional cuisine, and local activities.
They also participated in traditional games such as menarik upih (areca frond racing) and sampled local specialities, including buffalo curry.
Pulau Tuba has a population of about 5,000 and is one of the 99 islands that make up the Langkawi archipelago. — Bernama

Title: National unity minister says Orang Asal heritage part of Malaysia’s national identity, not separate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The heritage of Malaysia’s indigenous peoples (Orang Asal) is part of the country’s national legacy and identity, rather than belonging solely to the communities themselves, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said.
In a Facebook post marking the 2026 International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples today, he said efforts to empower indigenous communities should move in tandem with national development without allowing their languages, customs and traditional knowledge to become marginalised.
He said the country’s progress should provide more opportunities for indigenous youth to excel in education, the economy and leadership while preserving their cultural roots and identity.
“Malaysia is fortunate to have indigenous communities that are an important part of the country’s history and identity.
“The languages, arts, customs, traditional knowledge, relationship with nature and values passed down through generations are a significant part of Malaysia’s rich identity,” he said.
At the international level, Aaron said the United Nations (UN) recognised indigenous peoples as custodians and practitioners of unique cultural traditions and knowledge systems, including those related to environmental and biodiversity conservation.
According to him, in terms of national unity, indigenous communities are part of the Malaysian family, and the country’s diversity is a strength that shapes its identity rather than something that divides it.
“By respecting every community, preserving its heritage and valuing its contributions, we are building a more inclusive, harmonious and united country,” he said.
Aaron also urged all parties to renew their commitment to respecting indigenous identities, promoting their dignity and recognising their contributions to Malaysia.
“Their heritage is our shared heritage, and their identity forms part of Malaysia’s identity,” he said.
Observed annually on Aug 9, the International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples was designated by the UN General Assembly in 1994 through Resolution 49/214 to commemorate the first meeting of the United Nations Working Group on Indigenous Populations in 1982. — Bernama

Title: MBPP blames root rot and trunk cavity for Angsana collapse in George Town
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Root rot and a cavity in the base of a 90-year-old Angsana tree, compounded by chronic soil compaction and limited rooting space, contributed to its collapse along Jalan Macalister here today.
MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the 28-metre-tall tree, Pterocarpus indicus, had an estimated 30 per cent root rot, while cavity decay accounted for about 40 per cent of its base trunk.
“The collapse was caused by root rot estimated at around 30 per cent and base trunk cavities at about 40 per cent. These factors, combined with infrastructure upgrading works, chronic soil compaction, limited rooting space and the tree’s height, significantly increased the risk of structural failure,” he told Bernama today.
In the incident at about 9am, an elderly couple and their grandchild were injured when the Perodua Ativa sports utility vehicle (SUV) they were travelling in was crushed by the falling tree.
Rajendran said there were no reports of heavy rain or strong winds at or before the time of the incident.
He said MBPP began removing the fallen tree at 9.41am, with the road reopened at 2.20pm after clearing works were completed.
He said MBPP had assessed mature and aged trees along Jalan Macalister in 2024, resulting in 13 trees being identified for felling, all of which had since been removed.
He added that the last tree maintenance work along Jalan Macalister was carried out on January 29 this year, while a remote sensing study conducted last year found the trees along the road to be in good condition with no warning indicators.
He said 179 high-risk trees had been approved for felling this year, with 148 already removed, while 247 trees had been felled in the first three quarters.
MBPP says tree safety risks remain priority, especially those affected by works and restricted roots. — Picture via Facebook/Majlis Bandaraya Pulau Pinang
The trees were felled for various reasons, including obstructing drainage, being dead or leaning, posing a collapse risk, development projects, road and river widening, and encroaching on Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) pipeline alignments.
“For MBPP’s overall tree management programme, 2,535 trees were identified last year under various categories, including 45 cases involving drainage obstruction, 138 dead trees, 2,242 assessed under risk or other categories, and 110 linked to development or infrastructure works,” he said.
He said MBPP continues to prioritise trees posing safety risks, particularly those affected by infrastructure works and restricted rooting conditions.
“Following the incident, MBPP has instructed the appointed contractor to expedite work to reduce tree height and fell trees with potential collapse risks along Jalan Macalister, based on assessments by certified arborists,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak chokes under haze blanket as hot weather grips state until Aug 14
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 9 — Most parts of Sarawak will be experiencing hot weather and reduced rainfall until August 14, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip.
In addition, southern Sarawak is set to experience transboundary haze due to increased hotspots in the neighbouring country, he said.
“Analysis of the latest weather forecast models indicate that hot weather and below-average rainfall are expected in most parts of Borneo, including Sarawak, until August 14.
“The influence of southerly winds, combined with the anticipated high number of hot spots in the neighbouring country, could lead to transboundary haze and reduced visibility, particularly in southern Sarawak,” he said in a notice.
There are now eight locations in Sarawak where the monitoring stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. — The Borneo Post

Title: Terengganu police arrest three Myanmar men over sexual offence against disabled woman
Article:
CHUKAI, Aug 9 — Three Myanmar male refugees working as construction and cleaning workers were detained in connection with a sexual case involving an intellectually disabled woman in this district yesterday.
Kemaman district police chief Supt Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the three men, aged between 19 and 28, were arrested after receiving a report regarding the alleged sexual case from a 20-year-old woman on Friday.
“All three suspects have been remanded from August 8 to 12 to assist in the investigation. The investigation is still ongoing to identify other suspects who may be involved,” he said in a statement today.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 376 of the Penal Code.
He said the police need to fine-tune the investigation and to give sufficient space and time to the 23-year-old victim before completing the probe, considering that the woman is an intellectually disabled person.
In addition, Mohd Razi said his team also detected the spread of a video on the TikTok social media platform at around 8.30pm yesterday, showing a crowd gathering in front of the Kampung Enjin Gergaji Flats here following allegations of a sexual offence linked to the suspects.
He said that the public is advised not to make any baseless speculation as the case is still under police investigation.
“The police also advised the public not to take hasty actions against Rohingya refugees that could lead to criminal acts,” he said.
Members of the public who have information related to the case can contact any nearby police station or call 09-859 2222 to connect to the investigating officer, Inspector Mohd Hadaza Mat Amin. — Bernama
